title: 川の流れのように (Kawa no Nagare no Yō ni — Like the Flow of a River)
description:
Widely regarded as one of the greatest Japanese songs ever recorded, this 1989 ballad by 美空ひばり (Misora Hibari) is a moving meditation on life's journey. Lyrics by 秋元康 (Akimoto Yasushi) and music by 見岳章 (Mitake Akira). Released January 11, 1989 — just months before Hibari's death in June — the song became her swan song and sold over 2 million copies. It has ranked #1 in multiple polls for Japan's all-time favourite songs.

For learners: The vocabulary is moderate (N3–N4 level), with clear enka-style pronunciation and deliberate tempo that makes it ideal for reading along. Key words include: 知らず知らず (without realizing), 細く長い (narrow and long), 振り返れば (if one looks back), でこぼこ道 (bumpy road), とめどなく (ceaselessly), 黄昏 (dusk/twilight), おだやかに (gently/calmly), せせらぎ (murmuring stream). The recurring metaphor of a river (川) as a symbol of life's passage is central. The phrase 川の流れのように (like the flow of a river) appears as a refrain and is one of the most recognizable lines in modern Japanese popular music.
